How Do International Moving Companies Work?

When you need to relocate internationally, hiring a professional moving company should be at the top of your to-do list. Expert international movers can coordinate every aspect of your move from start to finish so you can focus on your new chapter abroad.

Relocation companies usually guide you through the process of ensuring your belongings are:

  • Properly documented for customs clearance
  • Packed securely
  • Transported safely
  • Delivered to your new home overseas

Why Moving Managers Matter

A moving coordinator starts the process by walking through your residence to create a detailed inventory and give you an estimate. Several companies have moved to a contactless model where you can use an app on your phone to perform the initial survey.

This professional is your go-to person for customs regulations and documentation requirements. They can also give you different transportation options for your belongings, such as air or sea freight.

Once you've agreed to the terms of service, the movers carefully pack all your goods using specialized materials to withstand international shipping. At this stage, your move manager should update you on all developments until the shipment is done.

What Additional Services Do International Moving Companies Offer?

Pet Relocation

Depending on the destination country, your pets may need to be quarantined upon arrival. Your consultant can guide you through this process, and companies like International Van Lines offer helpful resources to assist you too.

To ensure a smooth pet relocation, start planning early and work with your consultant to understand the specific health requirements, such as vaccinations and microchipping, for your pet's destination.

Choose a comfortable, appropriately-sized travel crate and acclimate your pet to it before the move to reduce stress during travel. If your pet has any special needs, discuss them with your consultant to ensure the best possible care throughout the relocation process.

Car Shipping

When shipping vehicles overseas, following tips for stress-free car shipping can help ensure a smooth process. If the new country's regulations don't require additional checks, the car may be taken directly to an inspection station for emission tests before being returned to the shipper.

To make the process easier, it's essential to research and prepare the necessary paperwork. Along with the title and registration, you might need an import permit, proof of ownership, and insurance.

Cleaning the vehicle and removing personal items can also help prevent delays during customs inspections. A good consultant will know each country's specific requirements for auto-shipping and can help guide you through the process.

How Much Do International Moving Companies Cost?

Based on extensive research into various service providers, we've found that most relocation companies can charge anywhere from $1,000 to $15,000. This doesn't include specialty items or full-coverage insurance.

These estimates depend on hugely varied individualized cases where several factors can determine the cost of your move. Key considerations include distance, type of freight (air, sea, or land), the weight of the shipment, and third-party contractors.

Additional Costs Involved in an International Move

Transporting your belongings is just one aspect of an international relocation. Additional fees can quickly add up, from arranging visas to securing storage options while you settle into your new country. Be prepared for these extra costs to avoid surprises during your move abroad.

Insurance

Don't overlook moving insurance when relocating to a new country. Transporting goods over long distances often leads to damage or loss. While most companies provide released value protection at $0.60/pound, this coverage may not be sufficient for your needs

To ensure your possessions are adequately protected, it's best to purchase full-value protection, even if it seems expensive. Our research revealed that many clients who skipped comprehensive coverage lost thousands of dollars worth of belongings.

Customs and Import Taxes

Customs and import taxes are another expense that adds to your international move bill. These fees are unavoidable and vary depending on the country you plan to relocate to, so having a moving manager discuss the ins and outs of this payment could be incredibly helpful.

Storage Costs

Storing your goods can also be a bit of a burden on your budget. A few of our top carriers include free storage for up to one month. However, most charge for storage from day one. Finding a moving company that includes complimentary options will always be preferable, so start your search early.

Quick Tips for Saving Money on Your Move

  1. Sell or give away things you don't use anymore.
  2. Throw away items that are broken and can't be fixed.
  3. Donate stuff you don't need to local shelters or the Salvation Army.
  4. Choose charities that offer free furniture pickup for donations.
  5. Use budget-friendly moving supplies and strategies.
  6. Pick a moving company that ships by sea instead of air—it's cheaper but takes longer.

» Take a look at our top 10 tips for saving money when you move.

How to Choose the Best International Moving Company for You

Check Reviews

Don't underestimate the power of reviews and testimonials from past customers. When you're dealing with transporting everything you own to a new country, you don't want to leave anything up to chance. Find out everything you can about a moving company's reputation before you choose.

Scour the internet and read both positive and negative accounts of people's experiences with various international moving companies. Look for patterns that might reveal a mover's strengths and weaknesses. Finding reviews that match your destination and move size can also be good practice.

Are they consistently praised for caring customer service and attention to detail? Or do you see recurring complaints about damages, delays, or hidden fees? These insights can help you separate the outstanding movers from the mediocre ones.

Get In-Home Surveys and Binding Quotations

Request in-home surveys and binding quotes from your top prospective companies. A reputable mover will send an expert to your home to carefully catalog your belongings and provide an all-inclusive price for your specific move.

Be wary of companies that want to give you a rough estimate for an unseen sight. These service providers often increase your bill once they've concluded operations and can keep your belongings as collateral. When it comes to international moves, pricing surprises are the last thing you want.

Ask All the Questions You Can

As you're getting quotes, don't hesitate to interview each company representative thoroughly. An exceptional moving team will patiently answer all of your questions, no matter how small or detailed.

They'll explain their processes for customs clearance, transit protection, storage options if needed, and how they handle any issues that may arise. A trustworthy company has nothing to hide and will be transparent about fees, insurance coverage, and credentials.

Confirm Licenses and Associations

Ensure that the company is licensed and insured for international moves and belong to reputable industry associations. For example, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) and the Federal Martime Comission (FMC).

You can check their complaint history and safety record through resources like the FMCSA or the Better Business Bureau. You can also verify if the moving company is legitimate by checking directly with the relevant associations or certification boards' websites.

Work With the Experts to Make Your Overseas Move Easier

Relocating abroad doesn't have to be a daunting experience. You can eliminate the stress and complexity of an international move by partnering with a professional service.

They'll handle all the logistics, paperwork, and coordination with overseas movers to ensure a seamless transition for you and your belongings. Trust full-service companies like Allied Van Lines or JK Moving Services to simplify the process and make your relocation a success.

How to Choose a Car Shipping Company

There's a lot to consider when choosing a reliable car shipping service. These factors can help you pick the best company for your needs:

Research Companies

Customer reviews and testimonials help you gauge a company's reputation and reliability. You can use sites like Trustpilot, Better Business Bureau, Yelp, Consumer Affairs, and Google. Additionally, you can ask trusted friends or family members about their personal car shipping experiences.

Reputation and expertise are also key factors to keep in mind. Companies with a proven track record, like these U-Haul alternatives, are likelier to have established processes to handle potential challenges.

Verify Licensing and Insurance

One of the best ways to check if a moving company is legitimate is to visit its website. Look for a valid Motor Carrier (MC) number issued by the US Department of Transportation (USDOT). This ensures the service is legally authorized to transport vehicles across state lines.

Additionally, check that the company has adequate insurance coverage of at least $100,000 per vehicle. Cargo insurance protects your vehicle against damage or loss during transport. In contrast, liability insurance covers any damage caused by the shipping service to third parties. 

Compare Pricing

Get quotes from multiple companies to compare prices. Be cautious of costs that seem too low, which may indicate poor service or hidden fees.

Each company has different packages. Based on the various service features, look for the option that'll give you the best value for your money. This can prevent you from overpaying for services you don't need.

Discuss Delivery Time

Some companies offer expedited shipping for an additional fee. For instance, if you're moving from New York to California, standard shipping takes seven to 10 days, while expedited shipping reduces the transit time to five to seven days. 

Prioritize Clear Communication

Choose a company that communicates clearly throughout the process and gives you a dedicated point of contact. A reliable service will inform you about your vehicle's status, such as when it's picked up, any transit updates, and the expected delivery date.

Keep Car Inspection in Mind

Ensure the company conducts thorough vehicle inspections before and after shipping to document any pre-existing damage. The scan should include a detailed report that notes the car's condition, including any dents, scratches, or other issues.

Consider Payment Methods and Discounts

Be cautious of services that demand significant upfront deposits. Most reputable companies will initially ask for a partial payment, with the remaining balance payable upon delivery.

Some may provide a discount for full upfront payment or cash transactions. Additionally, you can enquire about specific discounts for military members, seniors, students, or first-time customers.

Things to Consider When Shipping Your Car

Quotes May Be Adjusted

When you get a quote from a car shipping company, it might state something other than the expected fee. Prices may be adjusted for various reasons, such as fuel costs or demand. Always ask if the quote is subject to change and what factors might cause it to go up or down.

You Might Pay a Deposit

Most car shipping companies give you a free quote, but some might ask for a deposit when you book your shipment. This payment shows that you're serious about shipping your car.

Confirm the amount with the service and if it's refundable if your plans change. Some deposits are reimbursed before shipment or if your vehicle is damaged.

Shipping Dates Can Change

Book your car shipment with some flexibility in dates, as factors like weather or traffic can delay the transport. Inquire about the company's estimated delivery window and its policy for handling delays. Some services may offer a rental car if your vehicle doesn't arrive within a specified timeframe.

Confirm What’s Covered Under the Carrier’s Insurance

The shipping company should have insurance, but it may not cover all potential risks. Inquire about its specific policy and what it covers to understand who is liable in case of damage to your vehicle during transport.

This will help you determine if you need to purchase additional coverage, like gap insurance, to protect personal belongings inside your car during shipping.

Know Your Bill of Lading

The bill of lading is like a receipt for your car shipment. It shows crucial details like your car's condition, the pickup and delivery locations, and other special instructions.

It serves as evidence of the contract between you and the moving company. It'll also help you sort out any issues, like ownership or damages claims.

Ways You Can Ship a Car

By Truck

The primary method for shipping cars is via truck, with two main options: open and enclosed transport. Open transport, the most popular choice due to its cost-effectiveness, involves loading vehicles onto an open trailer exposed to the elements during transit.

Alternatively, enclosed transport gives you superior protection by securing cars inside a fully covered trailer, making it the preferred option for shipping luxury, classic, or high-value vehicles.

By Rail

Rail transport means increased speed and enhanced safety for your vehicle. Although rail shipping has benefits like less wear and tear during transit, it comes at a higher price point.

By Freight

Numerous cargo and freight companies focus on transporting vehicles to Alaska or Hawaii. They move cars from the pickup location to the port, where the vehicles are loaded onto a ship using either the Roll-On/Roll-Off (RoRo) method or securing them inside shipping containers for the journey.

If you're sending your vehicle to Oahu, car registrations must be completed within 30 days of arrival in Hawaii.

Delivery Options

Choose between door-to-door and terminal-to-terminal services. Door-to-door offers the convenience of collecting and delivering your vehicle at specific locations. In contrast, terminal-to-terminal is typically more affordable but requires you to leave and retrieve your car at designated shipping terminals.

What Do Car Shipping Companies Cost?

On average, it costs about $1,150 to ship your car in the US, but your actual price could be different depending on the following:

  • Distance: Short trips can reach over $1 per mile, while long trips might be as low as 50 cents per mile.
  • Pickup and delivery locations: If your pickup or drop-off location is far away or hard to reach, it can cost more due to the extra fuel and time to get there.
  • Seasonality: The season may cause shipping costs to fluctuate, with peak moving times like summer leading to higher prices when demand increases.
  • Transport type: Enclosed shipping gives more protection for your vehicle but costs more than open transport.
  • Vehicle operability: If you can't drive your car onto the carrier, the company must use special equipment to load and unload it, which can increase the price.
  • Pickup and drop-off dates: Prioritized scheduling might increase the cost if you need the company to pick up or deliver your vehicle on a specific date.
  • Vehicle size: The shipping expense may increase if larger vehicles or those with unique features need additional space on the truck or specialized accommodations.

10 Ways to Get the Best Car Shipping Price

Vehicle shipping can be expensive, but there are a few budget-friendly strategies to help keep moving costs down:

  1. Book early: Book your car shipment at least two weeks before you need it to avoid rush charges.
  2. Opt for open transport: This option is usually cheaper than enclosed options.
  3. Understand charges: Know your car's size, delivery spot, and carrier type to estimate costs.
  4. Negotiate: If you've compared quotes, you can use that information to get the perfect deal.
  5. Ship out-of-season: Summer is busier, so prices go up. Off-season shipping might get you discounts.
  6. Meet locally: Meet the carrier at an easy-to-reach spot instead of door-to-door to save on fuel costs.
  7. Terminal-to-terminal: This type of shipping can save on fuel and delivery expenses.
  8. Have flexible dates: Flexible scheduling lets you take advantage of cheaper shipment times.
  9. Group shipping discounts: Shipping several cars together can cost less per vehicle than transporting them separately.
  10. Referral discounts: If you refer someone needing car transportation services, you might qualify for discounts on your shipment.

Enjoy a Stress-Free Car Shipping Experience

Finding the right transporting company is essential and one of the only ways to ensure a stress-free car shipping experience. Each of the services on our list has its benefits, so check what others say about them, make sure the one you select has insurance, and try to book early.

International Van Lines has connections in over 140 countries if you want to move internationally. Alternatively, you can ask for Easy Auto Ship's professional help to inspect your car before you ship it. Then, you can relax knowing your vehicle is in good hands.

FAQs

Can I pack things in my car when I ship it?

Yes. You can generally pack personal or household items, such as clothing, bedding, and other non-perishable items.

Which is the best car shipping company?

The best shipping company for you will depend on your needs, location, type of automobile, and budget. Compare quotes from different companies to find the one that meets your requirements.

Does the AAA ship cars?

The American Automobile Association (AAA) doesn't offer vehicle shipping services, but it does provide its members with benefits like roadside assistance and insurance products.

Does your car get checked when you ship it?

Yes. When you ship your car, companies inspect your vehicle’s exterior to record its condition before shipping. Interior assessments are less common and typically only conducted if necessary. This process helps protect the transport company from false damage claims.

How do I not get scammed shipping my car?

Ensure the company is registered with the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration. Verify its business address, read online reviews, use traceable payment methods, and thoroughly read the contract.

Does your car have to be empty when you ship it?

No. It’s not illegal to have items in your vehicle during transportation, but many shipping companies require that your car be empty before transit for weight, safety, and liability reasons.

How long does it take to ship a car in the US?

Shipping a vehicle in the US typically takes one to two weeks, but the exact time can vary depending on distance, shipping routes, weather, and traffic. Some companies offer faster options for an additional cost.

Do you need vehicle insurance to ship a car in the US?

Yes, it's essential to have insurance when transporting a vehicle in the US to ensure that you're financially protected from any unforeseen incidents. Most reputable companies include insurance coverage as part of its services.

What is the difference between vehicle shipping and auto transport?

Vehicle shipping and auto transport are often used interchangeably to describe transporting a car from one location to another. However, "vehicle shipping" is often used for long distances or international moves, while "auto transport" typically refers to moving cars within a country.

Why Do I Need a Moving Company?

Most people have the same response when it comes time to move? Why do I need to hire a mover when I can do the work myself? There are many reasons why people choose to hire professional moving services. For example:

- Peace of mind

When you're moving house, there are a million and one things that only you can take care of. Moving isn't one of them. It's a lot easier to let someone else take care of the hauling, moving, and transporting. And it'll free you up to take care of the more important, technical details that only you can do.

- Reliability

What’s more, professional moving companies will have some sort of insurance on your stuff. So, if something breaks during the move, it’s covered. If you break something while moving it yourself, you’re out of luck.

- Time savings

What’s even more valuable than money? Your time. Hiring local movers can help you save a load of time. Sometimes, that’s worth the investment.

- More efficient

Everyone's good at something, but few people are good at EVERYTHING. You might be really good at what you do. But you know what the best moving companies are good at? That's right, moving. They'll know how to pack up, haul, and unload your stuff in the fastest, most efficient manner possible. So you can get on with your life and start living in your new home sooner.

- It’s safer

Moving can be hazardous to your health for many reasons. But one of the biggest ones is the strain you'll put on your body. Professional long-distance moving companies know how to move large, bulky, and heavy items without hurting themselves.

How Can I Find a Moving Company Near Me

Bottom line, it's a good idea to hire one of the professional local or long distance moving companies out there, but make sure that you are working with someone that services your area. This is easily done by looking at their website to see the coverage area. Local movers will have a smaller coverage area than the major long-distance moving companies. But the coverage area doesn't have to be large. It just has to include you.

Check on the moving companies' websites for a section like moving companies near me. You'll put in your address or zip code, and see what areas they cover. You can also search Google for "movers near me." Choose from the list to ensure you're getting a mover that works within your area.

How to Choose a Mover

The best moving companies will offer value-added services, good reputation, and insurance for your belongings. Here are a few important features you should look for during your quest for good and cheap moving companies:

- Reputation

Check out reviews online, ask around, and see if the company has a Better Business Bureau accreditation. A fair amount of good reviews will tell you that this company is worth investing in, will treat you well, and will get the job done right.

- Type of move

Are you moving locally or far away? Depending on the type of move, different moving companies will be more suitable for the task. If you're just moving around the corner or a few blocks away, local movers will be more price-efficient. On the other hand, if you're looking for a long trek, long-distance moving companies will offer you the most professionalism, along with the ability to move you farther.

- Amount of stuff

You also want to consider how much stuff you actually have to move. If you only have a small amount, 1 or 2 smaller appliances, etc., then you can opt for one of the cheap movers on your list. On the other hand, if you've got quite a bit of belongings to move, along with multiple major appliances, a more reputable moving service with insurance, is a safer bet.

What Is the Best Moving Company?

The best moving companies are the ones that fulfill your requirements, offer affordable pricing, and will work within your moving area. Those are the only things you really need to look for. It's also a good idea to check out the customer support experience. While this isn't always a necessity, it's nice to know that there's someone you can reach out to in case you have questions or in the event that something goes wrong before, during, or after the move. It is typically an excellent idea to read online reviews and hear what others have to say about a service, as well. This gives you an indication of the general quality of service you can expect from a moving company.

What is the Cheapest Moving Company?

Cheap moving companies are not unheard of. You just have to know where exactly to look. Start by getting a few online quotes. These are usually free, so don't pay for a quote. Once you've compiled a list of cheap movers, compare the different rates you received to find the most cost-efficient one.

But don’t just look at the price tag. After all, the best moving companies will offer added value on top of a standard price. That means they may be offering you more bang for your buck in the form of additional services, better coverage, or more flexible terms. So, don’t just pounce on the cheap moving companies. Weigh what you’re getting in the equation.

Also, bear in mind that cheap movers may not provide you with insurance. Often, the more professional movers will charge more because they come with the insurance and quality guarantee. If you're only moving a few items, insurance might not be that important to you, in which case, you should go with a cheap mover. But if you are moving valuable or expensive things, it's worth the investment to have an insurance policy in place.
